prompt: Build a stopwatch panel around a javax.swing.Timer: create a 50 ms timer whose action calls tick(), make tick() count into the "ticks" label, and make the "startStop" button toggle the timer. Follow the contract in the starter Javadoc exactly.
explanation: javax.swing.Timer is the Swing-safe way to run repeated work: it fires ActionEvents on the event dispatch thread at a fixed delay, so listeners may touch components freely. Separating the work into a tick() method gives two entry points -- the timer calls it in real use, and tests call it directly so they stay deterministic without ever sleeping. The button listener toggles with isRunning()/start()/stop(); the tests also fire the timer's registered action listeners by hand to prove the timer is actually wired to tick().
hints: Create the timer at the end of the constructor: timer = new Timer(50, e -> tick()); -- and do not call start() there.
tick() is plain state-plus-view code: count++; ticks.setText(String.valueOf(count));
In onStartStop, check timer.isRunning() -- call stop() if true, start() if false.
